correctness.rationale: On a largest Jordan block the different positive powers of the nilpotent part occupy distinct superdiagonals, so diagonalizability is equivalent to vanishing derivatives of orders 1 through q_j−1 at each node. Thus p'=FQ. In the degree-d space of real Q, the pairwise differences of outputs are linear functionals with monomial coefficients given by the displayed moments. If d<H one pair always collides; if d=H a finite union of proper hyperplanes cannot cover the real coefficient space (also when H=0). Multiplying F by one factor per interior sign change makes a nonzero constant-sign integrand, bounding the first nonvanishing moment by the number of such roots and proving finiteness. Hence the least degree and all inequalities follow, including H=0 for s=2 or all q_j=1. In the proposed sharp family, Jacobi orthogonality annihilates the endpoint moments below degree s−2, and the moment at degree s−2 is proportional to the nonzero weighted squared norm. An independent check with three size-two blocks at −1,u,1 yields full-span zeroth moment 4u/3; at u=0 the first moment is −4/15. The least degree is four for u≠0 and five for u=0. The general proof is analytic, not an extrapolation from the frozen rational-arithmetic checks.

value.rationale: This gives an exact obstruction to lowering the degree in a natural constrained matrix functional calculus, in a range not resolved by the usual Hermite upper bound. It predicts a degree jump when real spectral nodes move with the Jordan data fixed and gives a sharp upper envelope in every number of nodes. The moment formula is actionable from the nodes and block sizes alone, rather than a new name for derivative divisibility.
